title: A Complete Guide To In-wall Cisterns
bodyHtml:
Maximise Sleek with In-Wall Cisterns

Sleeker aesthetics are becoming increasingly popular for bathrooms everywhere, and there’s no better way to achieve the contemporary look than with an in-wall cistern system.

In this article, we’ll cover everything you need to know about concealed cisterns, their pros and cons, and why certain toilet technology trumps others.

What is an in-wall cistern?

In-wall cisterns, also referred to as ‘concealed cisterns,’ is a flushing system where the components and water tank is hidden inside your wall. Only the pan and push plate are visible, creating an ultra-sleek option for anyone striving for the modern bathroom look.

In-wall cisterns are available in two prominent actuation types: pneumatic and mechanical. Pneumatic flush actuators use small airs pumps, also known as billows, that are connected to hoses to flush the cistern. The advantage of this actuator is that you can install the in-wall cistern up to three metres away from the push plate.

Mechanical flush actuators differ from pneumatic, as they use rods to directly flush the cistern. These push plates are generally considered to be a little more reliable than pneumatic ones, as in rare cases, hoses in pneumatic installations can come loose. However, this is an easily fixed problem.

Why is an in-wall cistern so different?

There are a variety of aspects that set in-wall cisterns apart from regular toilets, including a modernised look, space saving design, ease of cleaning, and an increase in perceived value to your home.

Our Oli in-wall cisterns particularly standout due to their unique system - They are the only cisterns on the Australian market with a delayed refill valve, meaning water is not lost during the refilling process, saving around half a litre of water every flush!

This signals a proud move towards sustainable bathware practices and a great way to get bang for your buck when installing a new toilet.

The Pros of In-Wall Cisterns

Modernised Look

Concealed cisterns are a gorgeous choice for anyone chasing the contemporary bathroom look. The need for clunky, large traditional cisterns is negated with the entire system concealed behind the wall. This is instead replaced by sleek, minimalist pan and push plates to activate the flush, available in a variety of colourways to suit any bathroom vision.

Save Space!

In smaller bathrooms, traditional toilet suites demand more floorspace whilst installing a Wall faced or wall hung pan will reduce projection to around 500mm, earning back 100mm-150mm of precious bathroom floor space.

Increase Percieved Value

The inclusion of an in-wall cistern for your next bathroom reno is a surefire way to boost the perceived value of your bathroom. Renovators and house hunters are interested in the latest architectural trends, and bathrooms with concealed suites are becoming an increasingly popular sight. These suites are perceived as higher end, premium options, adding an air of modern sophistication to any bathroom.

What are the Cons of installing an In-Wall Cistern?

As with all new bathroom installations, there are some things to consider when deciding if an in-wall cistern is the right choice for you. As the system is installed within the wall, installation is pricier and these cisterns can be hard to access through tiled walls and could increase repair costs. This can be negated by having hidden access points in the wall.

In-wall cisterns also generally cost more for the components and fixtures vs a traditional back to wall suite.

Endless Styling Options

When incorporating an in-wall cistern into a bathroom renovation, the design possibilities abound. This versatile choice offers flexibility in both fixture selection and aesthetic customization.

The flush button selection presents an opportunity for personalization, with options ranging from various colors to metallic finishes. These buttons can seamlessly integrate into the overall design scheme, coordinating effortlessly with tapware and other bathroom accessories or blending discreetly into the tiled wall for a seamless look. With in-wall cisterns, the design possibilities are truly endless, allowing homeowners to create a bathroom space that reflects their unique style and preferences.
